real.claim: Setting: the TARGET belongs to a small formal logic defined in the context. Formulas are built from binary relation symbols applied to variables (variables are natural numbers), falsehood, implication, the universal quantifier and an operator K. K stands for Reinhardt's operator B, 'it is provable (known) that'. The logic is a fragment of Reinhardt's: it has no function symbols, constants, equality or arithmetic, and that limitation is declared separately. These definitions give the language (the new formation rule 'if p is a formula, so is Bp', over a purely relational first-order base), the defined connectives, and three standard syntactic notions: a variable occurring free; replacing the free occurrences of one variable by another variable; and one variable being free (substitutable) for another. Check in particular that the three syntactic notions are the standard ones and that substitution goes inside K.

Setting: the TARGET belongs to a small formal logic defined in the context. Formulas are built from binary relation symbols applied to variables (variables are natural numbers), falsehood, implication, the universal quantifier and an operator K. K stands for Reinhardt's operator B, 'it is provable (known) that'. The logic is a fragment of Reinhardt's: it has no function symbols, constants, equality or arithmetic, and that limitation is declared separately. These definitions give the proof system. 'All the usual schemas of logic' are rendered as: all tautologies (defined by truth assignments that respect falsehood and implication and treat atoms, quantified formulas and K-formulas as unanalysed), universal instantiation by a variable, distribution of the quantifier over implication, and vacuous quantification. The special axioms are Reinhardt's four. 'Universal closures' are rendered as: a schema under a prefix of universal quantifiers that leaves no variable free. 'Optionally prefixed by B' / 'Bp for each such sentence p' are rendered as: K of any such sentence is an axiom (Koellner's Σ ∪ KΣ). The only rule is modus ponens. The set T of extra hypotheses is not required to consist of sentences.

def PropVal (v : Form → Prop) : Prop := ¬ v fls ∧ ∀ φ ψ, v (imp φ ψ) ↔ (v φ → v ψ)
def Tautology (φ : Form) : Prop := ∀ v, PropVal v → v φ
inductive BaseAx : Form → Prop
  | taut {φ : Form} : Tautology φ → BaseAx φ
  | inst (x y : ℕ) (φ : Form) : FreeFor y x φ → BaseAx (imp (all x φ) (subst x y φ))
  | dist (x : ℕ) (φ ψ : Form) : BaseAx (imp (all x (imp φ ψ)) (imp (all x φ) (all x ψ)))
  | vac (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : ¬ Free x φ → BaseAx (imp φ (all x φ))
  | k2 (φ ψ : Form) : BaseAx (imp (K (imp φ ψ)) (imp (K φ) (K ψ)))
  | k3 (φ : Form) : BaseAx (imp φ (K φ))
  | k4 (φ : Form) : BaseAx (imp (K φ) (K (K φ)))
  | kall (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : BaseAx (imp (K (all x φ)) (all x (K φ)))
inductive Sig : Form → Prop
  | base {φ : Form} : BaseAx φ → Sig φ
  | gen (x : ℕ) {φ : Form} : Sig φ → Sig (all x φ)
def Closed (φ : Form) : Prop := ∀ x, ¬ Free x φ
def Axiom (φ : Form) : Prop := (Sig φ ∧ Closed φ) ∨ ∃ ψ, Sig ψ ∧ Closed ψ ∧ φ = K ψ
inductive Proves (T : Set Form) : Form → Prop
  | ax {φ : Form} : Axiom φ → Proves T φ
  | hyp {φ : Form} : φ ∈ T → Proves T φ
  | mp {φ ψ : Form} : Proves T (imp φ ψ) → Proves T φ → Proves T ψ
